commit_uploads.message:
config: move approvals out before --output overwrites the config it migrated

The reviewer's hold found a real defect. `--output` pointed at the config being
migrated wrote the migration over it, dropping `approved-commands`, and printed
a warning whose remedy — "to migrate them to approvals.toml, run
`wt config update`" — was false exactly then: the write had already removed
them, so the follow-up run reports `No deprecated settings found` and the
entries are gone.

`copy_approved_commands_to_approvals_file` had one production caller, the
in-place loop. That block is now `move_approvals_out_of`, and both writes that
land a migration on top of the config it came from call it — the in-place
update, and `--output` naming that same path. Any other destination leaves the
config alone, so its warning still names a `wt config update` with something to
migrate. "Write the path the user named" is no longer lossy.

`wt config create` on a dangling symlink reported `File exists (os error 17)`,
naming neither the path nor the link, right after the existence check said the
path was free. It now says what occupies it and what to do, as the rc-file
write already did, with the symlink case covered by a test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Release v0.79.0 (#4202)

0.79.0 was prepared and merged in #4181 but never tagged, so it never shipped.
Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock already carry the version, so this reuses it and folds
the thirteen commits that landed since into the same changelog section.

New entries cover the worktree-side rename fixes (#4190, #4191), the per-project
unknown-field warning (#4123), and the unterminated code fence in the picker's
preview (#4183, combined with #4178's column fix).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

config: write the path the user named, and check every config write the same way

`wt config update --output <path>` refused three things: the config being
migrated, an existing file without `--yes`, and an existing file with no
terminal to prompt on. A named destination is the user's choice — `cp` and a
shell redirect replace what is there — so all three go, along with the
no-clobber/clobber branch at the write. Pointed at the config being migrated it
writes the migration there; `approved-commands` still reach approvals.toml only
via the in-place update, which is what the warning above the write says.

`ConfigFile::edited` checked only one of its two candidate documents — the
as-written one — and `with_locked_mutation` then ran a weaker TOML-parse check
over whichever it got. Both candidates now face the same test, that the file
loads back as the config the mutation asked for, and the parse check goes. It
caught a mutator in the suite returning an edit it never made to the config
beside it, which previously wrote a file loading as something else.

Two write primitives stay, one per situation, so no call site picks between
them: a path the user named is written, a path wt observed absent is created
no-clobber. `wt config create` was on the wrong one, where a dangling symlink a
dotfile manager owns would have been replaced by a regular file.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
